issues.description: The return type of Stock.take(String) is inconsistent: the problem statement UML specifies take(String): int, the template Stock.java defines take(String) returning boolean, while the solution Stock.java defines take(String) returning int. This mismatch is structural and will confuse students implementing SealSaloon, because the intended logic (and the solution) expects an int return value (e.g., -1 to signal unavailable) but the provided template forces a boolean signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML and solution by changing the signature of Stock.take(String) in the template to return int. Update its semantics to return -1 when the ingredient is not available (or if not found) and otherwise return the remaining quantity after taking one unit. This makes the template consistent with the problem statement and the reference solution.

issues.description: The Stock.take method is described in the problem UML as returning an int (Stock.take(String): int) but the template implementation defines take(String) returning boolean. The solution implements take(String) returning int. This mismatch in the method signature/return semantics across artifacts creates a direct mapping and compilation confusion for students implementing SealSaloon logic that relies on the int-based contract described in the problem (e.g., checking for -1).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock.take method match the problem specification and solution by changing its signature to return int (e.g., return -1 when the ingredient is missing or unavailable, otherwise return the remaining quantity). Alternatively, update the problem/spec and solution to consistently use boolean semantics if that was intended. Prefer aligning the template to the problem UML (int) to avoid student confusion.
